title: Model names got more useful
summary:
This week made model choices clearer and text responses more predictable, while community builders found more ways to put image generation to work.

The `gemini` name now points to Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental, and text requests can use defined aliases. Other routes changed too: `openai-large` now maps to `gpt-4o-mini`, while `openai-reasoning` maps to `o1-mini`. Five Mistral configurations now advertise their existing image-input capability, and the Cloudflare-hosted DeepSeek distill model has its own name instead of sharing one with full DeepSeek R1. Names and metadata matter when they decide what an API client actually sends.

Most text models gained a Llama 4-derived conversational prompt, while specialized models kept their own instructions. POST cache keys now account for the entire request body, so changing a parameter such as `seed` does not retrieve a response cached for different parameters. Errors also preserve upstream HTTP statuses where available and present simpler details; model listings now return smaller OpenAI-style records.

The image feed editor now gets its model choices from the image API, with a loading state and a fallback list if the request fails. Six community additions showed what people are building around these tools: image-making apps, a WordPress image block, a Flutter/Dart SDK, a Discord bot with image and voice features, and an LLM podcast.

The text server stopped appending NSFW referral links to generated responses. Image feed events now mark prompts matching mature terms, and feed listeners filter mature and other restricted content from both replayed and new results. Streaming content-filter errors also have a clearer message and a `content_policy` flag.
